title: Cuando and mientras: what happened and what was going on

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando* and *mientras* from A2 Unit 13. *Mientras* + imperfect gives the background, what was going on during a long stretch of time. *Cuando* + preterite marks a single moment. Together they let you tell the story of a voyage.

items.spanish: Mientras los barcos cruzaban el Atlántico, los marineros tenían miedo.
items.english: While the ships were crossing the Atlantic, the sailors were afraid.

items.spanish: Cuando Colón desembarcó, tomó posesión de la isla.
items.english: When Columbus landed, he took possession of the island.

items.spanish: Mientras Colón exploraba las islas, buscaba oro.
items.english: While Columbus was exploring the islands, he was looking for gold.

items.spanish: Cuando los barcos llegaron a la isla, la tripulación llevaba semanas en el mar.
items.english: When the ships reached the island, the crew had been at sea for weeks.

sections.content: *Mientras* is followed by the imperfect when you describe two things going on together (*mientras cruzaban… tenían miedo*). *Cuando* is followed by the preterite for the event that interrupts or follows (*cuando desembarcó, tomó posesión*). Both words are written without an accent in these uses.
